title: pair, tuple and structured bindings
summary: Bundling values into pairs, how pairs sort, and reading them cleanly with auto [a, b].

sections.title: pair
sections.body:
✍️ `pair<int,int> p = {3, 5};` access with `p.first`, `p.second`.
✍️ Pairs compare **lexicographically**: first by `.first`, then by `.second`. So sorting a `vector<pair<int,int>>` sorts by first, breaking ties by second — for free.
✍️ `vector<pair<int,int>> v; v.push_back({val, idx});` is the standard way to sort values while remembering original indices.

sections.title: Structured bindings
sections.body:
✍️ `for (auto& [key, val] : mp)` iterates a map with readable names.
✍️ `auto [d, node] = pq.top();` unpacks a pair from a heap.

sections.title: tuple
sections.body: `tuple<int,int,int> t = {d, r, c}; auto [d, r, c] = t;` — useful for (distance, row, col) in Dijkstra on grids. Tuples also compare lexicographically.
